A retailer is modernizing a 15-year-old ESB that handles 900 integrations. Leadership wants a low-risk path to CP4I. Which strategy is MOST appropriate?

Strangler-fig migration: inventory and classify integrations, build a target pattern catalogue (API, messaging, event, file), migrate in value- and risk-based waves to fine-grained ACE runtimes and other CP4I capabilities, run old and new in parallel with routing at the edge, and retire legacy flows incrementally
Rewrite all 900 integrations before any go-live
Lift and shift the ESB unchanged into one container
Freeze the business for a year during migration
Incremental strangler migration reduces risk, delivers value early and allows learning. Pattern catalogues and inventory let migration happen in waves with parallel running.
Correct: incremental, pattern-led, parallel-run migration.
Wrong: a big-bang rewrite is high risk.
Wrong: keeps monolith problems and is not supported for many legacy stacks.
Wrong: unrealistic.
Wave 1 migrates 60 low-risk file and MQ flows; DataPower routes partner traffic to new or old implementations per API.
Large migrations: inventory -> patterns -> waves -> parallel run -> retire.

After a cluster-scoped CP4I installation, a second team installs the same capability operator in single-namespace mode in its own namespace. Both operators start reconciling the team's instances and fight over them. What went wrong?

Overlapping operator scopes: a cluster-scoped (AllNamespaces) operator already watches every namespace, so adding a namespace-scoped install for the same capability creates conflicting controllers; one scope model per capability must be chosen and enforced
The entitlement key is shared
The storage class is RWX
The Platform UI cache

Operators of the same capability must not have overlapping watch scopes. Mixing an AllNamespaces install with OwnNamespace installs for the same operator leads to duplicate reconciliation and conflicts.
Correct: overlapping operator watch scopes.
Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: unrelated.
The platform team removed the namespace-scoped install and documented a single cluster-scoped model.
Choose one installation scope model per cluster for each capability.
